Product Overview

Refined Canola Oil is produced from high-quality canola seeds and refined to a light taste, clear appearance, and stable shelf performance — suited for cooking, frying, baking, and industrial food processing applications. As a refined canola oil exporter and canola oil supplier for food manufacturers working across six sourcing origins, France AJ Alimentaire offers buyers flexibility on non-GMO canola oil bulk export, private-label packaging, and multi-origin blending options depending on destination-market requirements.

Why buy from a multi-origin canola oil supplier

Most canola oil exporters sell out of a single country, which means a buyer's supply is only as secure as that one harvest, that one port, and that one freight lane. As a multi-origin canola oil supplier and established canola oil trading company, France AJ Alimentaire sources refined canola oil across six countries so that a seasonal shortfall, a duty change, or a congested port in one origin does not stall a buyer's supply chain.

Lump or crushed sulphur is typically an intermediate industrial feedstock that requires further processing, whereas granular sulphur is sized and ready for direct field application, mechanical spreading and fertilizer blending. It is the everyday canned tuna of supermarket shelves, catering kitchens and ready-meal production.

Canned tuna is shelf-stable at ambient temperature. It ships in dry containers and is stored in ordinary warehouses, without the reefer equipment, cold-store capacity and power costs that frozen seafood requires — often the deciding logistics advantage for distributors in hot-climate markets.

Vietnam has built a substantial tuna processing sector around its central-coast fishing grounds, and canned tuna has become one of its fastest-growing seafood export lines. According to the Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP), as reported by Atuna, Vietnam’s canned tuna exports reached a record of around USD 299 million in the second half of 2024, with the US, Israel, Germany, Lebanon and Egypt among the largest destinations.

For B2B buyers, the practical reasons to work with a canned tuna supplier in Vietnam are:

  • Established export formats – 48-can cartons in the 140g–185g range are standard export packs, which makes comparison with other origins straightforward.
  • Market-ready labelling – the ANTAR Premium sheet shows English and Arabic labels, a combination widely used in Middle East and North African retail.
  • Origin diversification – buyers already sourcing from Thailand or other Asian origins can add Vietnam as a second source under one trading relationship.
  • Shelf-stable logistics – dry-container shipping and a long reference shelf life suit distributors serving long inland supply chains.

Product is sourced from producers operating under internationally recognized standards, including ISO 9001, HACCP and GMP where applicable. Wholesale Canned Tuna FOB and CIF Pricing

There is no fixed list price for wholesale canned tuna. France AJ quotes per carton at FOB (Vietnamese port of loading) or CIF (the buyer’s named destination port). Under FOB the buyer arranges ocean freight and insurance; under CIF those costs are included to the destination port.

The main factors that move a canned tuna FOB price per carton are:

  • Raw material – the world price of skipjack, which moves with catch levels and cannery demand
  • Pack style – solid generally prices above chunk, and chunk above shredded
  • Can size and drained weight
  • Packing medium and label requirements
  • Tinplate and packaging costs
  • Quantity and contract length – single shipment versus recurring monthly supply
  • Freight and destination – for CIF, the trade lane and discharge port

Promotional figures shown on product sheets are reference points only and are not an offer. Every quotation is indicative, moves with the world market, and is subject to destination port, quantity, packaging, freight, market conditions and final seller confirmation.

The number of cartons per 20ft or 40ft container depends on can size, carton dimensions, palletisation and destination payload limits. What Is IR 64 Parboiled Rice?

Parboiling typically involves soaking, steaming and drying rice before milling. Importers buying Indian IR 64 parboiled rice in bulk should specify both the variety and processing requirement, rather than requesting generic white or parboiled rice. This helps avoid comparisons between non-equivalent grades.

The promotional artwork includes a grain photograph and a measuring scale; the image is illustrative and does not establish a contractual average grain length. For technical purchasing, request producer documentation and agreed sampling criteria before signing an SPA.

Rice cost, vessel freight, insurance, loading arrangements, port conditions and available allocation may all change between offers.

CIF Conakry, Guinea: Shipping and Landed Cost

Under the standard CIF Incoterms rule, the seller contracts and pays for carriage and required cargo insurance to the named destination port. Risk generally passes to the buyer when goods are loaded on the vessel at the port of shipment, not when the vessel arrives at Conakry. The signed contract must state the governing Incoterms edition and named port.

A CIF price does not automatically include Guinea import duties, customs clearance, terminal charges that fall to the buyer, or inland transport. Importers should compare offers on equivalent product specifications and shipment terms, and ask their clearing agent for destination costs when estimating the full landed price.

Buyers planning one bulk cargo or a longer shipment program should state the target quantity, discharge requirements and required loading period in the RFQ.

  • Commodity trading companies: state whether the order is a spot cargo or phased supply program

LC 100% at Loading Port and DLC MT700 Terms

The promotional material states LC 100% at the loading port against documents and says DLC MT700 is acceptable. MT700 is the SWIFT message type commonly used to issue a documentary credit; it is not itself a separate payment guarantee. The actual credit must be issued by the buyer's bank with mutually accepted payment, presentation and documentary conditions.

Before issuance, buyer and seller should agree the beneficiary, issuing and advising banks, required documents, port names, latest shipment date, expiry, allowed partial shipments, and inspection conditions. The poster does not specify whether the credit must be confirmed or transferable, so those requirements should not be assumed from the image.

Depending on the contract, destination rules and bank requirements, the document set may include a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, inspection certificate, and any phytosanitary or food-safety documents required by the importing country.

These are documents to agree, not a representation that they were promised in the historical poster. Request the final list in writing before the bank issues the operative credit, and confirm acceptable inspection agency, timing and sampling method.

  1. Buyer company: registered name, country, authorised contact and importer details as applicable
  2. Product: Indian IR 64 parboiled rice, 5% broken

  4. Bagging: 50 kg PP bags and any printing, marking or palletization requirements
  5. Destination: CIF Conakry, Guinea, or another named discharge port for a new quote
  6. Delivery: requested first loading month and shipment schedule
  7. Specifications: any required moisture, grain size, quality limits, certificates and inspection method
  8. Banking: proposed 100% documentary LC procedure and buyer bank details for contract review

After reviewing the buyer's requirements, the commercial team can confirm whether a new offer is available, its applicable terms and the validity period. A price request by itself does not establish allocation or a binding contract.

  2. Review a current quotation stating price basis, shipment window, specification and expiry.
  3. Agree the SPA and verify the seller, documents and all commercial conditions.
  4. Arrange the LC only after the contract and bank documentary requirements are approved.
  5. Inspect and load the cargo in accordance with the contract and any agreed independent inspection.
  6. Present compliant documents for payment through the banks under the operative documentary credit.

France AJ Group presents a B2B sourcing guide for frozen chicken parts from China, covering chicken breast and chicken leg quarters for importers, frozen-food wholesalers, distributors and foodservice purchasing teams. The promotional material advertises 10 kg cartons (alternative packing on request), frozen storage at −18°C, a 12-month shelf life and LC payment at the loading port against documents.

The image also states “Price From $1,999 CIF”, but gives neither a unit of measure nor a destination port or validity period. It is not a confirmed USD/MT offer. Buyers should request a current, product-specific CIF quotation identifying the price unit, named discharge port and delivery schedule before making purchasing decisions.

China Frozen Chicken Parts: Wholesale Offer Overview

The two cuts pictured serve different commercial needs. Buyers should specify which cut they need instead of requesting a single undifferentiated “chicken parts” price. The table records the advertisement's stated terms; its claims are subject to formal seller and producer verification.

Frozen Chicken Breast vs Chicken Leg Quarters: What Buyers Should Specify

Chicken breast is commonly purchased by food processors, portioning operations and foodservice distributors, while leg quarters are requested by wholesale poultry distributors and buyers serving retail or hospitality channels. However, a photograph alone does not establish whether a cut is boneless, skinless, trimmed to a particular standard or within a particular piece-weight range.

For an accurate China frozen chicken breast wholesale or frozen chicken leg quarter CIF comparison, ask suppliers to quote the same specifications, carton net weight, shipment size and destination. A cheaper quotation for a different cut is not a like-for-like offer.

10 kg Carton Packaging and Frozen Storage at −18°C

The advertisement specifies 10 kg per carton or alternative packing at the customer's request. Buyers should confirm carton material, food-contact inner liner, net and gross weights, lot identification, language requirements, carton markings and palletization before contract signature.

The poster states keep frozen at −18°C and advertises a 12-month shelf life. These are promotional specifications rather than independently verified lot data. Request the manufacturer's label, production date, expiration date and required cold-chain controls; the remaining shelf life at delivery should be addressed in the contract.

Frozen poultry must be handled under an appropriate temperature-controlled supply chain, from origin cold storage through reefer loading and destination discharge. Buyers should arrange adequate refrigerated storage, container power and unloading capacity at the receiving port or warehouse.

China Poultry Export Eligibility and Destination Import Rules

Before requesting shipment, importers should check whether poultry products from China, the specific exporting establishment and the relevant product cut may enter the intended destination market. Veterinary restrictions, establishment approvals and documentary requirements can differ by country and may change.

The exporter and buyer should confirm the actual producer, establishment approval or registration as applicable, product origin and export health documents. Do not assume that an advertised HALAL mark or a general food-safety certification substitutes for governmental veterinary approval. Request written eligibility confirmation for the exact importing country before opening a bank instrument.

HALAL, HACCP, ISO and Veterinary Certificate Verification

The poster shows HALAL, HACCP, ISO, a health certificate and the statement “no hormones”. These are claims in the advertisement, not certificates supplied with it. For a compliant purchase, ask the trade team for documentation relevant to the producer, product and destination.

  • HALAL: issuing certification body, covered facility and product, certificate validity and importing-market acceptance.
  • HACCP / ISO: exact standard, certified establishment, scope and expiration date, where applicable.
  • Veterinary / health documentation: issuing authority and required certificate model for the destination.
  • “No hormones” statement: request an appropriate producer declaration or other substantiation rather than treating the logo as proof.
  • Product traceability: producer details, production lots, carton labels and mutually agreed inspection criteria.

Availability and acceptability of every certificate must be confirmed in writing for the nominated shipment and destination.

Frozen Chicken CIF Price: What the Advertised $1,999 Means

The promotional sheet displays “Price From $1,999 CIF”. Because no price basis (such as per carton or per metric ton), named destination port or validity date is provided, buyers cannot use that figure as a firm price benchmark. Request separate, current quotations for chicken breast and leg quarters.

Under CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight), the seller generally contracts carriage and the required insurance to the named destination port; the transfer of risk follows the applicable Incoterms rule and is not the same as delivery at the buyer's warehouse. Destination handling, import taxes, customs clearance and inland transportation should be evaluated separately.

For a comparable frozen chicken parts CIF quotation, ask for the full price currency and unit, named port, cut specification, carton net weight, shipment quantity, inspection terms, freight/insurance basis and offer expiry date.

Reefer Container Shipping, MOQ and Monthly Supply

The poster does not specify a minimum order quantity, container payload, loading port, monthly capacity or delivery lead time. These should be established through a formal offer, rather than inferred from a picture of a refrigerated shipping container.

For each proposed shipment, request the reefer-container type, permissible payload, cartons per container, net and gross cargo weights, loading temperature, pre-shipment inspection procedure and expected loading window. Buyers requiring a recurring programme should state the intended quantity per month and contract duration, so availability can be assessed against realistic production and shipping schedules.

Letter of Credit Payment and Shipping Documents

The advertisement states LC at the loading port against documents. Buyers and the seller must agree the issuing bank, whether confirmation is required, presentation period and documentary conditions in the final sales contract and letter of credit. The poster does not specify a complete MT700 instrument structure or guarantee bank acceptance.

A typical frozen poultry trade file may require a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, government veterinary or health certificate and destination-specific inspection or HALAL documents. The actual required list depends on importing-country rules and the LC terms; it should be agreed before issuance, not assumed to be included by default.

How to Request a China Frozen Chicken Wholesale Quotation

To receive a useful frozen chicken breast or leg quarter RFQ, submit the following information:

  1. Buyer: registered company name, country, contact and any required import authorization.
  2. Requested cut: chicken breast, leg quarters or separate quotes for both.
  3. Detailed specification: bone/skin requirements, piece-weight range, trimming, packing and grade standard.
  4. Quantity: total metric tons or containers, shipment frequency and contract duration.
  5. Cartons: confirm 10 kg net/carton or provide alternative packing requirements.
  6. Destination: exact discharge port, country and import approval requirements.
  7. Trade terms: request CIF to the named port and specify the quotation price unit.
  8. Documents: HALAL, health and other required certificates for the importing market.
  9. Banking and timing: proposed LC terms and preferred shipment month.
